rule: **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID | **C2 Resolution consistency.** ... An ID is never invented: a medium or high callee that names a member of a scanned module or type (`mod.T#f`, `mod.f`) is defined there, or is inherited from a base outside the scan.
source: KNOWN_GAP: methods from traits resolve to the using class at medium
notes: hello is defined once, in the scanned trait App\Greets → its ID is App.Greets#hello, and the call from the using class must use that ID (C1), high because it is defined in the scan. App.Person#hello at medium invents an ID (Person defines no hello and has no base outside the scan; C2) and lowers the tier. Inside the trait, $this->name() names the trait's abstract (body-less) App.Greets#name, high (Decision 2026-11-09). `use Greets;` is not a call. call_type: SPEC lists direct|method without defining them; this corpus uses method for every callee of the form Type#m / recv.m / .m (instance and static member calls) and direct for free functions, bare names and named nested functions.
